intent: A commentator telling the origin story over an Atlantic map: the ship crossing is the visual spine, the title count is the kicker.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which city hosted the FIRST Davis Cup in 1900?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which city hosted the first Davis Cup in 1900?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Boston. In August 1900, 4 Harvard students challenged Britain to a tennis match at the Longwood Cricket Club.

lines.direction: pull out to the whole North Atlantic: the British Isles light up dim, the Liverpool pin drops, the steamship route draws west and a ship sticker rides it to Boston; on 'lost' the US pulses and the sad GB flag-ball appears, the tennis ball sticker pops on 'grass'
lines.text: The British team crossed the Atlantic by steamship, and lost all 3 matches on grass.

lines.direction: back to Boston: the real Library of Congress portrait of Dwight Davis rises out of the United States on 'davis', the trophy sticker pops on 'trophy', the Longwood pin pulses in again on 'name'
lines.text: Dwight Davis paid for the silver trophy out of his own pocket, and the cup still carries his name.

lines.direction: wide Atlantic again, the title table grows in 4 rows over the ocean as each nation is named; the happy US flag-ball lands on 'nobody' with the trophy
lines.text: The United States has won it 32 times, Australia 28. Nobody else has reached 11.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: A student dare that never stopped. Follow us.
